candidates.source_name: ECEPP — EBRD Client E-Procurement Portal (notices, shortlists, contract awards)
candidates.why_relevant: Since 2019 all EBRD loan/grant-financed procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract-award notices for EBRD clients are published only on ECEPP. This is the single authoritative feed for Ukrainian bank and payment-infrastructure work financed by EBRD, including consultant selections that never reach Prozorro.
candidates.access_status: public browsing of notices; registration required to participate and possibly for full documents
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic scripted crawl of the notice-search results filtered by country=Ukraine and sector=financial institutions; capture displayNoticeId permalinks (e.g. viewNotice.html?displayNoticeId=...) and archive notice text plus award supplier names.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from ebrd.com procurement pages
queries_used: EBRD Ukraine bank digitalisation procurement notice consultant award

candidates.source_name: EBRD Technical Cooperation Project Summary Documents (TC PSD) — Ukraine financial sector
candidates.why_relevant: TC PSDs state the technical scope, beneficiary institution (e.g. NBU), consultant profile and indicative budget of donor-funded advisory assignments. Confirmed Ukraine-specific examples cover financial sector reform and a PMO at the National Bank of Ukraine supporting the Financial Sector Strategy — exactly the pre-procurement signal that precedes vendor selection.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the tcpsd listing and individual numeric PSD pages; extract TCRS number, disclosure date, beneficiary, scope and consultant requirements into a structured watchlist.
candidates.discovered_via_method: targeted search on ebrd.com project summary documents
queries_used: EBRD project summary document Ukraine bank "digital transformation" technical cooperation psd ebrd.com projects

candidates.source_name: EBRD project database (investment Project Summary Documents) — Ukraine financial institutions
candidates.why_relevant: Investment PSDs for Ukrainian banks (credit lines, risk-sharing, capital) disclose the accompanying technical-assistance components, which is where core-banking, digital channel and payments modernisation budgets sit. Also names the client banks, i.e. the buying institutions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Filtered crawl by country=Ukraine, sector=financial institutions; diff monthly for new disclosures.
queries_used: EBRD Ukraine bank digitalisation procurement notice consultant award

candidates.source_name: EBRD corporate procurement and consultancy services notices
candidates.why_relevant: Assignments contracted by the Bank itself (rather than by a client) — including sector studies and advisory work on Ukrainian financial infrastructure — appear here rather than on ECEPP. Complements ECEPP so the picture is not half-missing.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor page and any linked SMART by GEP notice feed for Ukraine/financial-sector keywords.
queries_used: EBRD Ukraine bank digitalisation procurement notice consultant award

candidates.source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — Ukraine procurement notices and contract awards
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes both procurement plans/notices and executed contract awards with supplier name, amount and date. Confirmed Ukrainian IT-vendor awards are visible here (e.g. computer equipment and EDMS licence awards to Ukrainian integrators), making this a direct vendor-identification route for World Bank-financed digital work.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the World Bank Projects & Operations API/data catalog dataset rather than scraping the SPA; filter country=Ukraine, sector=financial/ICT; capture procurement-detail OP-numbers.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball to data catalog
queries_used: World Bank Ukraine procurement notices portal "projects.worldbank.org" contract awards financial sector digital

candidates.source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Ukraine Project Appraisal Documents (PAD)
candidates.why_relevant: PADs and implementation status reports set out the technical architecture, component budgets and procurement plan for financial-sector and public-financial-management IT projects — the level of scope detail commercial announcements never disclose. candidates.why_relevant: Reaches private Ukrainian banks that never appear in public procurement: confirmed disclosures for UKRSIBBANK, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine and OTP Bank Ukraine risk-sharing facilities, each paired with an advisory component, plus advisory projects on credit reporting and digital financial services. negative_findings.description: No World Bank/IFC project in Ukraine dedicated specifically to 'payment systems modernisation' surfaced in search. The closest confirmed World Bank Ukraine appraisal precedent in the IT/financial-administration space is the State Tax Service Modernization Project (Report 25875-UA, 2003), and IFC's Ukraine payments-adjacent work appears as advisory projects (credit reporting, digital financial services) rather than a named payments programme.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched both seed phrasing and document-portal phrasing; found financial-sector rehabilitation DPLs, tax administration IT, and IFC risk-sharing/advisory disclosures, but no standalone payment-infrastructure operation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for this cell must not wait for a project named 'payment systems'; the relevant scope sits inside broader financial-sector, PFM and digital-government operations, so keyword rules need to be widened accordingly.

negative_findings.description: USAID's Ukraine financial-sector programme pages (as relayed by the NBU) describe workstreams but do not name implementing contractors or subcontractors, and no USAID-side award page for a payments-specific Ukraine programme was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Programme descriptions found for USAID Financial Sector Reform, Financial Sector Transformation and Investment for Business Resilience (IBR); none carried vendor/contract data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor identification for the US-funded slice must be done by joining programme names to federal award databases (USAspending) and oversight reports rather than from programme communications.

negative_findings.description: DevelopmentAid mirrors donor tenders and awards relevant to Ukraine but gates contractor and value detail behind a subscription.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public listing pages show title, donor, country and sector only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It can be used for discovery but cannot serve as the citable evidence layer; every lead must be resolved back to the originating donor portal.

negative_findings.description: No established Ukrainian-language term or portal was found for EBRD client-side procurement notices; Ukrainian coverage of EBRD tenders is journalistic or beneficiary-institution relay rather than a systematic Ukrainian-language notice feed. ECEPP itself appears to operate in English only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian queries returned ministry portfolio pages, news tags and one-off institutional announcements, not a Ukrainian notice register for IFI procurement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ukrainian-language monitoring for this cell must be alerting-based (keyword watch across gov.ua and media) rather than register-based, except for the МТД register and Prozorro donor module which are genuinely Ukrainian-language systematic sources.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live by me; all were taken from search-result metadata and snippets. Several (ECEPP notice permalinks, EU Funding & Tenders portal, TED) are JavaScript-heavy or session-bound and may present differently or 403 to naive crawlers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Liveness unverified by design; deterministic verification pass required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any 403/timeout on these should be read as bot defence, not as a dead source.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilateral donors and DFIs beyond the big four were not searched in this pass: KfW/DEG, SECO (explicitly named as an NBU partner), Sida, GIZ (implementer of EU4Business), Norfund/FMO/Proparco, and the Ukraine Development Fund vehicles. Several finance Ukrainian bank modernisation directly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over KfW, SECO/SIFEM, GIZ and DFI (FMO, Proparco, DEG) Ukraine financial-sector project databases and their tender pages, in both English and German/Ukrainian where applicable.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI accountability, evaluation and audit layers were not systematically mapped — EBRD Independent Evaluation Department, World Bank IEG, IFC CAO, and EU Court of Auditors reports. These retrospectively disclose what was actually delivered, by whom, and what failed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an evaluation-documents sweep filtered on Ukraine + financial sector / digital, and treat evaluations as the ground-truth check against procurement-stage announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: Consultant-side self-disclosure was not mined: the firms winning IFI banking/payments assignments (management consultancies, Big Four, specialist payment advisers) publish project references, and their staff publish assignment detail on professional profiles. This often reveals scope and duration that the notice omits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a consultant watchlist from confirmed awards, then monitor their Ukraine project-reference pages and press releases; note that professional-network scraping raises ToS issues and should be manual.

coverage_gaps.description: Ukrainian-language searching in this pass covered ЄБРР, МТД, Prozorro donor procurement and NBU/USAID project naming, but not Ukrainian terms for IFC (МФК), World Bank (Світовий банк) or EIB (ЄІБ) combined with payment-infrastructure vocabulary (платіжна система, СЕП, еквайринг, миттєві платежі).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up Ukrainian-language pass on МФК/Світовий банк/ЄІБ + платіжна інфраструктура, СЕП, миттєві платежі,core banking terms, and cross-reference the МТД register hits.

coverage_gaps.description: ECEPP notice permalinks appear to be non-guessable (displayNoticeId / accessCode style), so no reliable listing-to-detail enumeration strategy was established in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether ECEPP exposes a filterable search results endpoint or RSS that yields stable notice IDs; if not, plan for an authenticated registered-supplier account to obtain systematic coverage, subject to ToS review.

brief: Ukraine's donor-financed banking and payments modernisation is documented through two parallel stacks that must both be tracked. The IFI stack is English-language and supply-side: EBRD's ECEPP portal plus TC/investment Project Summary Documents, the World Bank's projects and documents portals, the IFC Disclosure Portal (which uniquely reaches private banks such as UKRSIBBANK, Raiffeisen and OTP Ukraine via risk-sharing facilities with paired advisory components), and EIB TA calls that surface on TED. The Ukrainian stack is demand-side and local-language: the statutory МТД register of registered technical-assistance projects with attached procurement plans, the Prozorro donor-procurement module opened in 2023, and NBU/Ministry of Finance programme pages that name donors and workstreams. The weakest link is vendor attribution: IFI and USAID programme communications routinely describe scope but not the contractor, so award-level identity has to be reconstructed by joining these registers to USAspending, TED award notices and oversight reports; ECEPP's non-enumerable notice IDs are the main structural obstacle to systematic collection.
